kf: Ring-shaped (**annular**) rashes have many causes: **tinea** (scaly active edge), granuloma annulare (no scale), erythema migrans, urticaria, pityriasis rosea herald patch, erythema multiforme, discoid eczema, subacute lupus, psoriasis, sarcoidosis.
Key questions: **scale?** (where), duration of each lesion, itch, symptoms, sun exposure, tick bites, drugs.
Scale at the advancing edge with central clearing: scrape for fungus before steroid.
Trailing scale inside the edge: pityriasis rosea or erythema annulare centrifugum.
Annular lesions lasting <24 h: urticaria; >24 h with bruising: urticarial vasculitis.
myths: **"Every ring is ringworm"**: granuloma annulare and other rings are commonly mistaken for tinea.
patho_lead: Rings form when a process **spreads outwards while the centre heals**.

mech.t: Fungi, bacteria or immune activity move outwards; the centre resolves.
Active inflammation and organisms sit at the edge.
mech.cap: Granuloma annulare (smooth, no scale) versus tinea (scaly edge).

mech.t: Leading-edge scale (tinea) vs trailing collarette (pityriasis rosea).
